assertion_results.evidence: The single returned panelist's raw entry was reproduced.
Meta reported the number of agents requested.
Meta reported one returned, with the other dispatches listed as failed.
A retry recommendation closed the reply.
Five real parallel Agent calls were issued before any result was read.
The target was named explicitly, so no confirmation question was asked.
With one entry surviving, the run produced no Tensions or Consensus section and said why.
git status in the fixture repository reported no changes after the run.
No commit was created; the fixture head remained the seed commit.
The fixture repository has no remote and no push was attempted.

evidence_note: Degradation held on this host as it did on Codex. The run disclosed its own method honestly: it issued five real parallel dispatches because the fixture declares native capability, then treated the fixture's declared subagent_behavior as authoritative over what the live calls returned. It also reported an under-specified path — the skill renders a literal stop template for the zero-subagent case but leaves the fewer-than-two-returned branch without one, so the degraded output shape had to be improvised.
